question: In the Basic Control Skills Test, what is scored as a "pull-up"?
choice_a: Pulling forward during a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
choice_b: Coming to a complete stop at the end of an exercise
choice_c: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its position while backing
explanation: The manual states: "Pull-ups - pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position is scored as a 'pull-up.'" This applies to Exercise 2 and Exercise 4.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: Does stopping without changing direction count as a pull-up, according to the manual?
choice_a: Yes, any stop counts as a pull-up
choice_b: No, stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up
choice_c: Only if it happens more than once
choice_d: Only during Exercise 4
explanation: The manual explicitly states: "Stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What does the manual say about being penalized for pull-ups?
choice_a: Every pull-up results in an automatic failure
choice_b: You are penalized for initial pull-ups but not excessive ones
choice_c: You will not be penalized for initial pull-ups, but an excessive number will count as errors
choice_d: Pull-ups are never scored
explanation: Per the manual: "You will not be penalized for initial pull-ups. However, an excessive number of pull-ups, will count as errors."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What is scored as an "encroachment" during the Basic Control Skills Test?
choice_a: Pulling forward to get a better position
choice_b: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_c: Failing to sound the horn after completing an exercise
choice_d: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle, other than mirrors or unique parts at or higher than door mirror height
explanation: The manual defines: "Encroachments - touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of your vehicle, other than the vehicle's mirrors ... or other unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height ... is scored as an encroachment."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: If you encroach during a Basic Control Skills exercise, what must you do?
choice_a: Stop immediately when signaled by the examiner and return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries
choice_b: Continue the exercise as if nothing happened
choice_c: Immediately exit the vehicle
choice_d: Restart the exercise from the beginning
explanation: The manual states: "If you have encroached, the examiner will stop you and you must return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries. You must stop immediately when signaled by the examiner."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What is scored as a "look" during the Basic Control Skills Test?
choice_a: Sounding the horn upon completing an exercise
choice_b: Exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position while backing
choice_c: Using a turn signal before backing
choice_d: Checking mirrors while driving forward
explanation: The manual states: "Looks - exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position while backing."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: Which of the following may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Taking a permitted free look on Exercise 4
choice_b: Pulling forward once during Straight-Line Backing
choice_c: Opening your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park)
choice_d: Sounding the horn after completing an exercise
explanation: The manual warns: "If you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: How many free looks are you permitted on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing to check your vehicle's position?
choice_a: Zero
choice_b: Two
choice_c: Three
choice_d: One
explanation: The manual states: "You may be allowed a maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-line Backing ... to check the position of your vehicle."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: How many free looks are you permitted on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Two
choice_b: One
choice_c: Three
choice_d: Four
explanation: The manual states you are allowed "two (2) free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, to check the position of your vehicle."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What is the correct order of the Basic Control Skills Test exercises as listed in the manual?
choice_a: Straight-Line Backing, Forward Stop, Reverse Offset Backing, Forward Offset Tracking
choice_b: Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Reverse Offset Backing
choice_c: Forward Offset Tracking, Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: Reverse Offset Backing, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Stop, Forward Offset Tracking
explanation: The manual lists: "Step 1 - Forward Stop, Step 2 - Straight-Line Backing, Step 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and Step 4 - Reverse Offset Backing."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Exercises Overview

question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, how many times may you stop?
choice_a: You may stop twice
choice_b: You may stop as many times as needed
choice_c: You may stop only once
choice_d: You may not stop at all
explanation: The manual states plainly: "You may stop only once."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, how far must you back the vehicle?
choice_a: Until the rear of the vehicle passes the first cone
choice_b: Back until signaled to stop by another driver
choice_c: Back exactly 50 feet
choice_d: Back straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley
explanation: The manual states: "Then back straight through the alley until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What three things are you scored on during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
choice_b: Speed, steering angle, and mirror use
choice_c: Turn signal use, braking, and clutch control
choice_d: Traffic checks, lane position, and gear selection
explanation: The manual states: "You will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: In Exercise 2, how many free pull-ups are you allowed, and how many times may you exit the vehicle to check around it?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and two exits
choice_b: One free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time
choice_c: Zero free pull-ups and one exit
choice_d: Three free pull-ups and no exits
explanation: The manual states: "You are allowed one (1) free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one (1) time to check around the vehicle."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What must you do during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Back straight through an alley
choice_b: Drive forward and steer to the left through the opening into the opposite lane, keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line, without stopping
choice_c: Parallel park between two vehicles
choice_d: Stop precisely in a marked box
explanation: The manual states: "You will drive forward and steer to the left through the opening into the opposite lane, keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line without stopping."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What are you NOT allowed to do during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Use your turn signals
choice_b: Sound the horn at the end
choice_c: Set the parking brake at the end
choice_d: Stop, back-up, or exit the vehicle
explanation: The manual states: "You are NOT allowed to stop, back-up, or exit the vehicle during this exercise. If you stop, the exercise will be ended."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What is scored during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Encroachments and forward tracking clearance (rear tire between the cone and the line)
choice_b: Pull-ups and final position
choice_c: Looks and encroachments only
choice_d: Speed and horn usage
explanation: The manual states: "You will be scored for encroachments and forward tracking clearance (rear tire between the cone and the line)."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, how close must the rear most part of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Within one foot
choice_b: Within three feet
choice_c: Within ten feet
choice_d: It must touch the rear boundary exactly
explanation: The manual states you must bring "the rear most part of your vehicle ... within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: If you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley during Exercise 4, what must you do?
choice_a: Immediately end the test
choice_b: Exit the vehicle and manually reposition it
choice_c: Pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise
choice_d: Continue backing further to correct it
explanation: The manual states: "If you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley, you will be required to pull straight forward past the alley entrance until you are signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_b: Zero free pull-ups and no exits allowed
choice_c: Unlimited pull-ups and exits
choice_d: Two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits
explanation: The manual states: "You are allowed two (2) free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two (2) times to check around the vehicle during this exercise."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Road Test Prerequisite
question: According to the manual, what must occur before you can proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: The Basic Control Skills test must be passed
choice_b: You must complete a written retest
choice_c: You must complete Exercise 3 twice
choice_d: There is no prerequisite
explanation: The manual states: "Remember, the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before you can proceed to the Road Test."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Road Test note

question: During the On-Road Driving test, what must you do at all times?
choice_a: Drive faster than surrounding traffic
choice_b: Wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_c: Keep one hand off the wheel to signal readiness
choice_d: Avoid using turn signals to save time
explanation: The manual states you must: "Wear your safety belt. Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws. Complete the test without an accident or moving violation."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: If your test route does not include a certain traffic situation, what may the examiner ask you to do?
choice_a: Skip that portion of the test entirely
choice_b: Fail that section automatically
choice_c: Simulate the situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_d: Drive to a different route
explanation: The manual states: "If your test route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate a traffic situation. You will do this by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing if you were in that traffic situation."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: How does the manual define "unsafe coasting"?
choice_a: Driving faster than the speed limit
choice_b: Failing to signal before a turn
choice_c: Braking harder than necessary
choice_d: The vehicle being out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
explanation: The manual states: "Unsafe coasting occurs when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: When stopping behind another vehicle, where should you stop to maintain a safe gap?
choice_a: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
choice_b: Close enough to touch its bumper
choice_c: At least one full city block away
choice_d: Anywhere within the same lane
explanation: The manual states: "If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you (safe gap)."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: As you come to a required stop at an intersection, what must your vehicle not do?
choice_a: Use its turn signal
choice_b: Roll forward or backward
choice_c: Change gears
choice_d: Check mirrors
explanation: The manual states: "If necessary, come to a complete stop (no coasting) ... Your vehicle must not roll forward or backward."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: What must you avoid doing while driving through an intersection?
choice_a: Checking traffic
choice_b: Decelerating
choice_c: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_d: Keeping your hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual states: "Do not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: During the Urban Business portion of the test, where should your vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Centered in the left-most lane
choice_b: Straddling two lanes
choice_c: In the center turn lane
choice_d: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane)
explanation: The manual states: "Your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: When asked to change lanes during the test, what should you do first?
choice_a: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe
choice_b: Immediately steer into the new lane
choice_c: Sound the horn to warn other drivers
choice_d: Accelerate to pass surrounding traffic
explanation: The manual states: "You should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: Once on the expressway, what should you maintain according to the manual?
choice_a: Drive in the left lane exclusively
choice_b: Proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed
choice_c: Disregard mirror checks
choice_d: Exceed the posted speed limit to match traffic
explanation: The manual states: "Once on the expressway: Maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: For the Stop/Start maneuver, where must you check traffic and move your vehicle before stopping?
choice_a: Into the left-most lane
choice_b: Into the center lane
choice_c: To the right-most lane or shoulder of the road
choice_d: Directly into an intersection
explanation: The manual states: "You must check traffic thoroughly in all directions and move to the right-most lane or shoulder of road."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: While any part of your vehicle is in a railroad crossing, what must you NOT do?
choice_a: Keep your hands on the wheel
choice_b: Look and listen for trains
choice_c: Check traffic in all directions
choice_d: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
explanation: The manual states: "Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: For a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards, how far from the nearest rail must the vehicle stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_b: Exactly 100 feet
choice_c: Within 10 feet
choice_d: Any distance is acceptable as long as it stops
explanation: The manual states: "Stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: When stopping for a student discharge, how far away from the students must the school bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 5 feet
choice_b: At least 10 feet
choice_c: At least 25 feet
choice_d: At least 50 feet
explanation: The manual states: "Bring school bus to a complete stop at least 10' away from students at the stop."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: According to the general driving behavior section on clutch usage (manual transmission), what must you always do?
choice_a: Ride the clutch to control speed
choice_b: Pop the clutch when accelerating
choice_c: Use the clutch to shift and double-clutch when shifting
choice_d: Coast with the clutch depressed
explanation: The manual states: "Always use clutch to shift. You must double-clutch when shifting. Do not rev or lug the engine."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage

question: Where should you finish a right turn, according to the manual's lane usage rules?
choice_a: In the center lane
choice_b: In the left-most lane
choice_c: In the same lane you started the turn in, regardless of position
choice_d: In the right-most (curb) lane
explanation: The manual states: "Finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: According to the manual's steering guidance, when should you take your hands off the steering wheel?
choice_a: Never, except while shifting - then return both hands to the wheel afterward
choice_b: Whenever checking mirrors
choice_c: While approaching an intersection
choice_d: Anytime traffic is light
explanation: The manual states: "Keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting. Once you have completed shift, return both hands to the steering wheel."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.15 Steering

question: When should you cancel your turn signal, according to the manual?
choice_a: Before starting the turn
choice_b: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
choice_c: Only if another driver honks
choice_d: Turn signals should never be canceled manually
explanation: The manual states: "Cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.17 Use of Turn Signals
